title: Customer Canvas: Activation Hypotheses — Xenith Health POC
content:
Purpose
-----
This doc captures our initial activation hypotheses for the Xenith Health POC: what we will test, the measurable success criteria, required inputs, and the lean workshop agenda to align technical and product stakeholders. Treat as living — expect edits after the kickoff workshop.

Context & high-level outcome
--------------------------
Xenith Health wants to embed real-time clinical note summarization and triage suggestions into their provider workflow. The POC aims to demonstrate:
- that Redwood’s hosted/dedicated stack can meet latency and throughput requirements for a live in-clinic demo,
- the extraction quality is clinically useful (precision over noisy EHR snippets), and
- an economic signal: cost per triage suggestion is materially better than an internal lambda-based baseline.

Activation hypotheses (what we expect to prove)
------------------------------------------------
1) Latency SLO hypothesis: using Continuous Batching + prefix caching on a dedicated pool, median end-to-end generation latency for a 300-token summary will be <= 180ms for 95% of requests in-station.
2) Quality hypothesis: Summaries will achieve an average ROUGE-L >= 0.55 against the clinical-curated gold set and clinician-rated usefulness >= 4/5 on a 20-sample blind review.
3) Cost hypothesis: With quantized weights + adaptive batching, per-inference token cost will be <= 60% of Xenith’s current baseline for similar outputs.
4) Reliability hypothesis: Under synthetic burst load (x10 baseline QPS for 30s), automatic fallback to a smaller model preserves availability with graceful degradation (reduced length) and no customer-facing errors.

Concrete acceptance criteria (measurable)
----------------------------------------
- Latency: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 180ms for 300-token summaries measured over a 24‑hour demo window on Dedicated.
- Throughput: sustained 30 qps on a single reserved GPUPool configuration without queuing above 150ms.
- Quality: ROUGE-L >= 0.55 and clinician usefulness mean >= 4/5 on a 20-case review.
- Cost: end-to-end cost per request (compute+network) <= $0.20 for the target prompt/response size.
- Stability: <1% 5xx errors during the stress run; fallback correctness (shortened summaries) meets basic coherence checks.
- Security: PII redaction pipeline validated on sample dataset; SOC2-relevant controls exercised for data-in-transit.

Scope (in)
----------
- Implement data ingestion adapter for Xenith’s mock EHR stream (FHIR-like JSON) and a simple redaction step.
- Deploy a dedicated Redwood GPUPool with required model variant and quantization profile.
- Provide a lightweight frontend stub for provider demo (React component, sample flow).
- Run evaluation harness: automated ROUGE/L and human clinician review.

Scope (out)
-----------
- Full production integration with Xenith’s SSO or full EHR system (out of scope for POC).
- Complex audit log retention and long-term compliance packaging (we will surface requirements but not implement full retention policy).
- Multi-region failover testing (single-region demo only).

Key milestones & timeline (2-week sprint POC)
--------------------------------------------
Week 0 (Prep, 3 days): align data schema, receive sample EHR snippets, confirm remote demo station connectivity.
Week 1 (Build): ingest adapter, redaction, model selection, deploy dedicated pool.
Day 8: internal perf run and smoke QA.
Week 2 (Eval & Demo): human review, cost analysis, customer demo + retrospective.

Roles & responsibilities
------------------------
- Solutions Eng (owner): Priya — overall POC lead, integration, and demo run.
- ML Eng: Daniel — model tuning, quantization profile, perf runs.
- Product Eng / FE: Asha — demo UI and sample flow.
- Customer lead: Dr. Sara Nguyen (Xenith) — clinical reviewer and acceptance approver.
- Security reviewer: Marcos — redaction checks and quick compliance review.

Data & access checklist
----------------------
- Sample data: Xenith to provide 200 de‑identified encounter excerpts by Nov 14.
- Access: SSH bastion + demo model API key (scoped) — solutions eng to create.
- Data handling: all samples stored in POC bucket with lifecycle 30 days.
- Redaction: implement the built-in PIIDetector + custom regex for MRNs.

Experiment matrix & evaluation plan
----------------------------------
We will run a small matrix to compare tradeoffs:
- Model variants: base-large vs base-small-quantized
- Batching: none vs adaptive batching 50ms window
- Caching: none vs prefix/KV cache for repeated preambles
Measure: latency distribution, tokens/sec, ROUGE-L, clinician usefulness score, cost per request.

Workshop agenda (90 minutes)
---------------------------
1) 5m: Introductions & success alignment (Priya)
2) 10m: Xenith clinical priorities and demo story (Dr. Nguyen)
3) 20m: Data shape + redaction requirements (Marcos + Xenith SRE)
4) 25m: Architecture review and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated) (Daniel)
5) 15m: Acceptance metrics and evaluation plan (Asha)
6) 10m: Risks, open questions, and next steps (all)

Risks & proposed mitigations
---------------------------
- Risk: Sample data contains unexpected PHI patterns.
  Mitigation: Add immediate stop-gap regex rules; escalate to Marcos.
- Risk: Dedicated pool capacity shortage during demo.
  Mitigation: Pre-book burst capacity and validate failover model variants.
- Risk: Clinician reviewers delayed.
  Mitigation: Run automated ROUGE/L and recruit 2 backup clinical SMEs.

Open questions (to resolve in kickoff)
------------------------------------
- Does Xenith require persisting full transcripts for 30+ days or can we store derivatives only?
- Which internal baseline cost number should we use for the cost hypothesis? (Xenith infra team to provide)
- Is there a list of disallowed terms or framing that must be avoided in summaries?

Quick demo script (for in-clinic flow)
-------------------------------------
1) Provider clicks "Summarize" in EHR sidebar.
2) Frontend submits note excerpt to Redwood POC endpoint.
3) Model returns 2-paragraph summary + triage tag (urgent/normal).
4) UI highlights suggested actions; provider rates usefulness (1–5) — sampled for evaluation.

Deliverables at POC close
------------------------
- Performance report (latency/throughput/cost) with configuration used.
- Quality report (ROUGE + clinician reviews).
- Demo artifact: frontend stub, sample data, runbook for model config.
- Short decision memo: recommended next steps (dedicated commit, private deployment, or halt).

Immediate next steps (before kickoff)
------------------------------------
- Priya to confirm sample data arrival and create demo API key (by Nov 14).
- Daniel to spin a perf branch and pre-select model candidates (by Nov 15).
- Asha to scaffold demo UI and sample flows (by Nov 16).
- Schedule 90m kickoff with Xenith stakeholders (target Nov 18).

Notes to self / TODOs
---------------------
- Add quick script to anonymize timestamps in samples.
- Prep 10-minute recording of architecture for sales review.
- Track ENG-4791 for infra changes needed.

End of doc — update after kickoff with agreed answers and final acceptance thresholds.
